description: Overview of events produced by Tetragon Enterprise (part of Isovalent Platform). It's designed to give users insights into Tetragon operations and workloads activity, and help configure things like resources or export filters.

options.content:
Tetragon generates different types of events, depending on the policies loaded.
Events are then exposed via gRPC API and exported to a JSON log file.

This dashboard provides an overview of events generated by Tetragon.
It's intended mainly to help configure Tetragon and design a data pipeline consuming these events.

Before events are exported to a JSON log file, they pass through export filters,
meaning that the volume of exported events might be significantly smaller than the volume of generated events.
See the "Export Insights" section for a comparison.
For details on filtering, refer to [Tetragon Events Export Documentation](https://docs.isovalent.com/operations-guide/tetragon/configuration/export.html#filter-exported-tetragon-events).

For description and examples of each event type, refer to
[Tetragon Events API Reference](https://docs.isovalent.com/user-guide/reference/events/index.html).

options.content:
Most Tetragon events are associated with a process.
Events are annotated with the process node and binary, as well as Kubernetes metadata: namespace, workload, pod.

This section highlists clusters, namespaces, workloads, nodes and binaries with the highest rate of generated events.
If you spot an outlier, you can select it in dashboard filters to see drill down by event type.

Note: since events metrics can have high cardinality, Tetragon allows you to configure which metric labels are enabled
(see [documentation](https://tetragon.io/docs/installation/metrics/#configure-labels-on-events-metrics)).
If relevant labels are disabled, this section will show limited information.

options.content:
Tetragon events are typically exported to a JSON log file.

This section provides an overview of the exported data.
Metrics shown here are total counts for the selected cluster(s) - they don't recognize other filters.

Large volume of exported events might lead to high infrastructure cost and make it harder to extract valuable insights.
Common solutions include configuring export filters and rate limiting.
For guides on these refer to [Tetragon Events Export Documentation](https://docs.isovalent.com/operations-guide/tetragon/configuration/export.html).

Tetragon alerts (AlertRules) trigger alerts based on evaluation of events against CEL expressions.

This section provides insights into the alert' operation and resource usage. 
Metrics shown here help monitor the volume of generated alerts and their exported data.

Large volumes of exported alert data might impact storage requirements and downstream processing.
Monitor these metrics to ensure your alert configuration is efficient and properly sized.

For guidance on configuring alerts, see the [Tetragon Alert Rules Documentation](https://docs.isovalent.com/operations-guide/tetragon/alerts/).
